title.narrative: Digital livelihoods? The online gig economy and the future of decent refugee work in cities

description.narrative: Research and development activity contributing to the UK’s strategy to address key development challenges.

This project aims to have a positive impact on the future of decent refugee work in the online gig economy, with a focus on refugees in urban areas. Lebanon – an Upper Middle Income Country – will thus directly benefit from the outcomes of this project. Secondly, due to the high numbers of forcibly displaced persons from Syria currently living in Beirut, and the resulting relevance of this project for this particular population, the project will also be indirectly beneficial to Syria, and directly beneficial to Syrians living in exile. The labour markets in urban areas of Lebanon have been under severe pressure since the Syrian mass displacement, resulting in restrictions on Syrian labour to a limited number of economic sectors. Access to fair and just work is thus very scarce for Syrian refugees in Lebanon. Yet, ‘Decent Work’ is a key pillar of the global sustainable development agenda, with particular endorsement by the International Labour Organization, with which this project collaborates. At a time of widespread mass displacement with uncertain economic futures for many displaced families and individuals, the need for decent work as a key component of sustainable development necessarily includes the need for fair and decent work among registered refugees. By looking at the particular risks and opportunities that are provided by the growing online gig economy in Beirut among refugees, this project is directly relevant to key development challenges of Lebanon, with special regard to displaced persons living in the country. Secondly, digital labour may provide new opportunities for linking informal refugee labour with a positive impact on displaced persons’ re-integration in the home country, once safe return has become possible. The project is therefore directly relevant to the development challenges a post-crisis Syria will be facing, especially in terms of its labour market and its economy. The activities and outputs, and the pathway to impact this project follows, are designed to promote more just and equitable forms of economic development in Lebanon and beyond, mainly through offering a better understanding of the development-related impact of digitally mediated refugee labour. The project will contribute to better labour market policies that take refugees’ complex economic lives into account. Though its outputs and partnerships (with the ILO), it will also reach diverse policy actors and seeks to influence their policies through research. One example for this is the production of a policy paper in collaboration with the ILO, with a focus on just digital refugee work.
